setting.note: A soldier ten years gone from the Trojan war spends ten more years fighting the sea to reach one small Ionian island; the poem's fixed point is real Ithaca, but the wanderings that fill it belong to a mythic Mediterranean whose stops scholars have argued over for centuries.

rights.originalWork: Ancient Greek epic attributed to Homer, composed around the eighth century BCE and long out of copyright. Mapped as a cited work: no text stored, no passages reproduced. The places are facts and the notes are our own.
rights.textSource: None stored. A cited book reproduces no text.
rights.territoryNotes: Locations and original commentary only. No reproduction of any text, in any territory.
rights.attribution: The Odyssey, attributed to Homer. Locations mapped by Read the Places; traditional identifications are noted as such.

palette.note: The wine-dark Aegean the whole poem is spent crossing. A cited book's colour is not a quotation; it still has to be legible, and this clears WCAG AA on paper.
